items.title: Frank Foster — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History
items.q: I think I wrote one or two arrangements for the Andrew Johnson band.

ctx.x: Just a few things about the Jack Jackson band. What was their repertoire? What were you playing?

We had lots of stock arrangements that were bought in the music store, and a few special arrangements that were made by one or two members of the band. Not too many. I think I wrote one or two arrangements for the Andrew Johnson band. That’s the band I said that had the Lunceford-type approach.

Jack Jackson’s band was more patterned after the Basie band. We had lots of Basie stock arrangements, the book. It’s Sand, Man!, Wiggle Woogie, One O’Clock Jump. All those things that were made -- 9:20 Special. Almost everything that the Basie orchestra became known for back in the late ’30s and early ’40s, the Jack Jackson band played.
